Commentary.Commentary: Right then! 649 is India's total. Windies need to make at least 450 or play out 60-70 overs to make India bat again. Case 2 could be a possibility but even that seems like a mountain to climb. Join us back shortly...

Hard work for the bowlers. It is an understatement. Devendra Bishoo picked up 4 wickets but at the cost of 217 runs. Chase got to his century as well while Keemo Paul's injury hurt Windies badly. They were looking down and out on Thursday itself and the situation has worsened a lot.

If Day 1 did not have enough massacre, Rishabh Pant came out this morning and started hitting from the word go. But he agonizingly fell short of his ton while his captain got his. Then, when everyone felt that Jadeja was wasting time in the middle, he came out with a century of his own, his maiden in Tests. Awww... feather beds... these pitches.

The game started with Shannon Gabriel dismissing Rahul on a duck but then, it was all India. Shaw and Pujara counter-attacked with a double century stand with the latter missing out on a ton. The 18-year old got to his though. Then, Kohli and Rahane piled on more misery.

Okay then. India do not get bowled out. On a flat batting track in Rajkot, they have had 3 centurions, a 90, an 80, a 40, 2 double digits, 2 single digits and a duck. A paradise. This is their 6th highest total at home and second best, batting first in their own backyard.
NOW INDIA DECLARE! Short and outside off, Shami punches it towards sweeper cover and crosses over. Kohli decides that enough is enough and calls his men back. TEA HAS BEEN TAKEN AS WELL.

Ha ha ha! Virat Kohli is smiling. He actually wants to signal about the declaration but Jadeja is not seeing him at all! Kohli waits, watches Jaddu finish his celebration and then gets ready to signal. But like a proper Test batsman, 'Sir' puts on his helmet, puts on his gloves and then gets ready to see what happens on the next ball! He is not even looking at his captain! Kohli is sheepish now and starts to laugh.

Actually, given the way the Windies are bowling, the Indians need not do anything fancy. Runs are coming quite easily. Join us back at 1210 local (0640 GMT) for the second session.

Well, feeling pity for the Windies bowlers. After a wicket in the very first over, they have simply struggled to put any pressure on the batsmen. This morning just seemed like the players have come because they have been rostered on a fielding shift and simply went through the motions. Kohli and Pant took full toll of that and made runs at will. At one point of time, it seemed like the wicket-keeper would go past his skipper but eventually, the captain got to his ton, with Pant narrowly missing out. The dominance of Pant is clearly seen in that 133-run stand with Kohli, where he scored 92.

142 runs, 29 overs, 1 wicket. Another passage of play dominated by the hosts. Pant has been the only loss, that too, perhaps due to a rush of blood. Many players love to get to milestones with a biggie and he seemed to get consumed by that.

Tossed up on off, driven politely to long off for a single.
Devendra Bishoo comes to roll his arm over.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and straight, watchfully defended.
Another close shave! Short and outside off, Pant looks to cut but it goes uppishly. Luckily for him, it does not carry to point.

OOPS! Nearly drags it on! Full and around off, Rishabh comes forward to defend. But then, the ball hits the bottom part of the bat and perilously rolls back onto the stumps! Good reflex action from RP to try and deflect the ball away but then he realizes that it was a bit away from the sticks.
SIX! This is going, going, gone! Tossed up once again and out comes Pant once more. This time he is to the pitch of the ball. Smashes it over long off.

FOUR! Not quite cleanly hit but effective. Full on off, Pant dances down the track, is not quite to the pitch of the ball but still goes through with his shot. It goes off the inner half but clears mid on comfortably.

Drinks break. That's the end of the first hour of play. India have managed to add 53 without losing a wicket. The Windies bowlers seem to be struggling as the batting pair is scoring quickly without taking any risks. Can we expect more fireworks after the break?
Full and outside off, watchfully pushed to cover.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Down the leg side, a touch short. Pant initially looks to pull but then bails out. Shane Dowrich dives full length to his right and stops it.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

SIX! MAIDEN TEST FIFTY FOR PANT! This comes after the brilliant century in the final Test against England. A length ball, around middle and off, Pant swivels and whips it mightily over mid-wicket! Not much of a celebration but a stern piece of instruction from Kohli. Probably trying to calm him down. Do not gift your wicket away.

EDGED, FOUR! Streaky from Pant. Not a bad line, not a bad length, from Keemo Paul. Full and outside off, a touch wide, Pant goes for the drive but there is minimal footwork. Gets an outside edge which goes past the man at gully to the third man fence.
Kohli has flicked the ball off his pads to mod-wicket.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. One run added to the total.
A fuller ball on off is driven crisply to long on for a single.
Tossed up ball, played to mid-wicket.
Flighted ball on middle and off is tucked into the mid-wicket region to get a single.
Tossed up ball, defended off the front foot by Pant.
Fuller ball driven to mid on, no run.
In the corridor of uncertainty, Kohli comes forward to keep it out.
The Indian skipper has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Pants taps this full ball into the covers region to get off strike.

A very full ball around off, Pant tries to absolutely bludgeon it straight down the ground, but the southpaw looses his shape and mistimes it to back to the bowler. Paul gets a hand to it to deflect it to mid off.
Paul, from around the wicket, keeps it very full around off, Pants drives this softly into covers.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman.
Tossed up delivery on off, Kohli drives it to mid on.
The batsman has driven it through mid on.
Flighted ball on off is crisply driven to sweeper cover for a single.
A fuller delivery is defended by the southpaw.
Tossed up on off, driven to mid on.
Roston Chase into the attack now.
A full ball is pushed through covers for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Pant flicks this full delivery on his pads straight to the fielder at square leg.
First loose shot from the Indian keeper, Keemo dishes this on a length just outside off, Pant tentatively looks to play at it but misses it completely.
A fuller ball on off is played to mid on by the attacking southpaw.
Starts well with a good length ball from around the wicket with a bit of inward shape on it, Pant plants his front foot forward to block it out.
Keemo Paul comes into the attack.
Pant works it down the leg side. They pick up a single. 400 up for India.

Shorter of a good length ball on Pant's body, the keeper tries to flick it but gets a leading edge and the ball lobs to the left of the bowler. Lewis tries to catch it with his left hand but the ball is wide enough for the southpaw to continue batting.
Pant tries to pull this marginally short of a good length ball, he is a bit early into the shot as he gets a bottom edge and the ball rolls into the slip region.
A shorter of good length ball is punched to covers.
Good ball by Lewis, he bangs this one short and gets the ball to rise onto Pant, the southpaw gets on his toes to play it down towards the gully region.
Lewis starts the new over with a good length ball around off, Pant blocks it off the front foot.
A length ball angling in is tucked into the mid-wicket region by Kohli to end the over.
A bit shorter of a good length around off, played to the point region by the southpaw. They pick up a single.
Gabriel from around the wicket dishes this one way outside off, Pant shoulders arms.
FOUR! Lovely Shot! Superb batting from Rishabh Pant as he flicks this very full ball on his pads through mid-wicket to get four runs.
A bit shorter this one shaping into Kohli, he tucks it through the mid-wicket region to cross over.
FOUR! Fabulous flick from the Indian captain, a full ball on his pads is flicked through mid-wicket for a superb boundary.
FOUR! 50 partnership comes up as Pant instinctively pulls this short of a good length ball angling into his body very fine to beat the fielder at fine leg and gets a boundary to end the over.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
A shorter of a good length ball is defended off the back foot by Kohli.
Just short of the fielder at deep square leg, Pant pulls this short ball but gets a top edge. The fielder at deep square stops it from crossing the fence. One run added.
A bit shorter of a good length around off, punched to covers.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Better from Gabriel as he lands this one on a good length around off, Kohli comes forward and keeps it out.
Length ball on the pads is flicked to deep square leg to add a run to the total and get his captain on strike again.
Fractionally short of a good length angling into Virat's body, the Indian skipper pushes it to mid-wicket to get a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! Quintessential Virat Kohli. 3000 runs for the Indian captain in India. A gorgeous cover drive to this length ball on off get to that landmark.
Fires this down the leg side. Pants gets inside the line and leaves it alone.
Good batting this by the Indian captain as he works this length ball into mid-wicket and gets off strike.
A very full and fast delivery on off, Kohli drives it back to the bowler.
The Indian skipper has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Marginally short of a good length, Kohli pushes this one to the point region and gets a brace for it.
A bit shorter of a good length on directed towards Pants body, the attacking keeper taps it down into the square leg region to get a quick single.
Full and on off, Kohli gets forward and defends it back to the bowler to end the over.
A short ball angling into Pant's body, the southpaw tucks it into square leg to get off strike.
A fuller length delivery on middle and off, Kohli pushes this into the mid-wicket region to change strike.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Good bounce there for Shannon as he keeps it a bit shorter of a good length just outside off, Kohli lets it go watchfully.
Gabriel starts off with a very full length ball wide of off, Kohli looks to play at it but the ball goes under his bat and to the keeper.
Shannon Gabriel will bowl from the other end.
Fuller delivery on off, Pant leans forward and drives through covers to get a brace.
Wide of off this, Pant tentatively looks to play at it but misses.
FOUR! What a start for Pant. This is the advantage of the right hand - left hand combination. Keeps it on a fuller length but strays on his pads. Pant flicks it for a boundary through square leg.
This time Lewis gets it right and lands this length delivery on off, with an inward shape on it. Kohli pushes it into mid-wicket and gets off the mark for the day.
A bit shorter of good length this but too wide of off to entice Kohli into a shot, Kohli shoulders arms.
Starts with a wide delivery outside the off stump, Kohli leaves it alone.

We are all in readiness for play to begin as the umpires and the Windies team walk out to the middle. The Indian pair of Virat Kohli and Rishabh Pant stride out with the skipper taking strike. Sherman Lewis will start the proceedings for the visitors.

Hello and welcome all to our coverage of Day 2 of this first Test between India and West Indies being played at Rajkot. After a magnificent century on debut by young Shaw, India find themselves in a dominating situation right from Day 1. The current pair of skipper Virat Kohli and Rishabh Pant will look to put up a big first innings total and put the Windies bowlers under pressure. West Indies, on the other hand, will be keen on breaking this partnership and enter the Indian tail at the earliest. How can the visitors stop the Indian skipper and the flamboyant keeper-batsman from taking the match away from them? Yesterday we did not see a lot of assistance for the bowlers. Will the second new ball do the trick for the tourists? We are surely in for an exciting day of Test cricket. Stay tuned...
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

We're done with today's action. Do join us on Friday for Day 2 which promises to be run-filled as the pitch will be at its best for batting. The Windies will need to be more disciplined in their approach if they want to stay in the hunt. Tune in at 0930 local (0400 GMT) for all the action. Cheers!

For India, the early loss of KL Rahul was the only moment when they would have felt any pressure. After that, the double century partnership between Shaw and Pujara forced Windies into submission and then the pair of Rahane and Kohli further inflicted the damage with a century stand. Pujara and Rahane would be gutted though for missing out on a golden opportunity to get big runs under their belts. Anyway, Virat Kohli is still out there, unbeaten on 72, and will be eyeing a daddy hundred. We can expect fireworks with Rishabh Pant around and there is still enough batting left for the home team to push their total in excess of 500.

A day to forget for Windies. It was mentally and physically tiring for them. Apart from the first five overs or so, their bowlers didn't get much assistance from the deck and looked listless on the whole. Not only did they fail to pick wickets, they conceded runs at a brisk rate too. The ploy to keep fielders in the deep allowed the batsmen time to rotate the strike with ease which didn't let any pressure build. Shannon Gabriel was decent in his first couple of spells but apart from him, the others have struggle written all over their spells. Devendra Bishoo was a major disappointment, if one has to pinpoint a single bowler.

Prithvi Shaw, the 18-year old, says that he is feeling really good now, after the century but before that, he was pretty nervous, he admits. Stresses that he has got lots of runs in domestic cricket but was trying to remind himself to forget all that. Agrees that he did think that it was his first Test innings and he had doubts about how to play but then as he got into the groove of things, he decided to play according to the merit of the delivery. On his century celebration, Shaw says that he was remembering his father as the latter has sacrificed a lot for the youngster's career. On his maturity in cricket, Prithvi says that he has played a lot of cricket right from the age of schooling and has gained a lot of experience from all those. On his disappointment after losing his wicket, Shaw says that he is definitely not happy with his score on this track as it is a good wicket to bat on. Adding further, he says that it was the last over before Tea and he could have avoided that shot, though he later admits that the stickiness on that delivery after bouncing did him in.

The day belonged to a young 18-year boy - Prithvi Shaw. There was so much build up leading to his debut and the young man handled all the pressure with ease. He played some extraordinary shots, particularly off his back foot, and showed why he is touted as the next big thing in Indian cricket. It was a truly entertaining knock where many found a mixture of Sehwag and Tendulkar in his style of batting. Plenty of records got demolished in his very first Test innings and the most notable one was him becoming the second youngest Indian to score a hundred. A star is born. Truly. Let's see what he has to say as Sanjay Manjrekar is down with him for an interview.

Another session dominated by India as they end the first day of this Test match in the driver's seat. The evening session saw 38 overs bowled where India lost the wicket of Ajinkya Rahane but also scored 132 runs in it. The current Indian batting pair is leaving the ground, looking satisfied with their progress.
A length ball angling away from the batsman, Pant strides forward and pushes it to point. That's it, Stumps on Day 1.

Gabriel switches to over the wicket for the penultimate ball of today's play. Lands it on a good length around off, Pant taps it down to cover-point, looks for a run but Kohli has shut his shop for Day 1. Dot.
Gabriel pulls out of his delivery stride as Pant was not ready.
A length delivery on middle, Pant flicks it with great timing past the diving mid-wicket fielder for a couple of runs.

SIX! Not in control but it has gone all the way! Gabriel digs in a short delivery, well-targeted at the batsman, doesn't matter to Pant if the close of play is just around the corner. He goes on with his pull shot, doesn't get it away off the meat of his blade but it still flies over fine leg for a biggie. First of the innings and it has come in the last over of the day.
Back of a length delivery on off, Kohli drops it with soft hands to point and scampers across to the other end.
A length ball angling into the batsman, Pant flicks it in front of square leg and takes a single.
1 more minute left on the clock. So, we can get one more over today. The overrate has improved drastically in this session with spinners bowling relentlessly from both ends.
Chase drops it short and outside off, Pant slaps it to deepish cover and takes a single.
Quicker this time, full and on off, 92 kph, Pant defends it back to the bowler.
Full and flighted on off, it's driven through the line and Chases moves across to his right to make the stop.
Slightly short and around off, hurrying up a bit onto the batsman, Kohli forces it out in the gap at covers for a run.
Flighted full ball on off, Kohli defends it back with a dead straight bat.
Shortish and wide outside off, punched through covers for a single.
Oohhh... this one stays low after landing on a length around off, Kohli does well to keep his eyes glued to the ball as he keeps it out from the bottom half of his bat.

Once again there is big movement for Gabriel with the second new nut. Kohli tries to defend it from the crease but it jags back in and strikes him on the back thigh. The impact is so hard that his handkerchief flies out and falls beside the stumps.

Big movement there. But it bothers the keeper more than the batsman. Gabriel hurls it on a good length around off, Kohli makes an easy leave and after going past him, the ball moves in massively. It puts Dowrich's agility to full test who passes it with flying colours. Nice athleticism to dive across to his left to collect the ball.
Bowls it on a good length and wide outside off, an easy leave for Virat.
Width on offer outside off, Kohli dabs it fine down to third man and takes a couple of runs.
In the channel outside of, Kohli lets it to the keeper.
Defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flatter and on off, Pant defends it off his front foot.
Quicker and on middle, a slider, Pant defends it to the leg side.
Loopy and on off, Pant defends it off his front foot.
Full and on middle, knocked down towards mid on for a run.

Four byes! As if the Indian batsmen aren't scoring enough themselves that Windies are helping them with gifts like these. Chases fails to grip the new ball and fires it way down the leg side. Kohli lets it be and Dowrich has no chance of stopping it. A boundary at fine leg.

Some issue with the second new ball already. A bit of a scratch mark on the new cherry. Looks like someone has taken a bite of the apple. Anyway, they have replaced it. Roston Chase to continue from this end...
FOUR! Gabriel tries to test the new batsman with a short delivery around leg. Pant swivels inside the crease to get under the bounce and pulls it fine down the leg side for a boundary.
Angles it in around off, Pant keeps his eyes on the ball and defends it on the leg side.
Off the mark! A length ball on off, Pant works it off the inner half of his bat to deep mid-wicket for a couple of runs.

Good length ball on middle and off, Rishabh blocks it off his back foot. Kohli is seen saying something to Pant with a smile and Rishabh also flashes his smile in response. Sorry, not good in lip reading.
Gabriel switches to 'round the wicket and slips a length ball down the leg side. Pant tries to flick but misses.
Shortish and outside off, Kohli eases it down to third man and takes a single.
Second new ball has been taken. Shannon Gabriel returns to make the first use of it.
Flighted and on off, driven to extra cover. A successful over for Windies.
Skidding in from around off, Pant keeps it out off the inner half of the bat to mid-wicket.
Tossed up ball on off, Pant defends it off his front foot.
Birthday boy, Rishabh Pant walks in next. He has turned 21 today. Will like to make it a memorable year for himself, starting from today.

OUT! There is some spike on the Snicko and Rahane has to walk back, another start wasted by him. Windies are delighted. They have got a wicket against the run of play. The move to not opt for the second new ball and continue with the old one has provided them a breakthrough. Chase is the one to break this 105-run stand. Not a delivery to brag about though. It's short and wide outside off, begging to be dispatched. Rahane obliges as he goes deep inside the crease with a square cut. But he fails to middle his shot and Dowrich immediately jumps in joy after collecting the ball. They appeal and the finger goes up. Rahane has a chat with his skipper who seldom says no to a DRS-taking opportunity. The replays roll in and Snicko puts everything to rest. Waste of a review, none left for India now. Now then, something that will worry Rahane. Three of his last four dismissals have come against the spinners. A chink in his armour?

Huge shout for a caught behind. The finger has gone up. Ajinkya Rahane walks up to his skipper, has a chat with him and then signals for the DRS. Wonder why? He must be knowing whether he has edged it or not. Let's find out.
Quicker one, bowled in the flatter trajectory around middle, Rahane defends it off his front foot.
Flighted and around leg, Kohli flicks it past mid-wicket and crosses for a run.
Loopy and on leg, it's defended off the front foot by Rahane. End of a quick over, don't think it took even a minute.
Flatter and shorter on middle, Kohli moves back and eases it to deep mid-wicket for one.
Quicker and fuller on middle, clipped straight to mid-wicket yet again.
Leans forward to a full ball and blocks it safely.
Gets forward and across to help it with the spin to short mid-wicket.
Flighted and on leg, flicked on the leg side but straight to mid-wicket.
Full ball on middle and leg, it's flicked past the square leg fielder for a single.
Flatter and shorter on off, Kohli stands back and helps it to square leg.
Turns it off his pads to the leg side, finds mid-wicket.
Another off drive by Rahane, this time he knows that he has played it with soft hands. Calls his partner as soon as he hits it and scampers across for a single.
Full and on off, driven down to mid off and Rahane immediately turned down the single.
Flighted and on middle, Kohli takes his front leg forward and flicks it with the spin to deep mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
100-run stand comes up! Full and flighted on middle, Kohli knocks it down to long on for a run. They continue to grow from strength to strength.
Another flick shot, this time from the bat of Rahane. The ball rolls in front of square leg and they steal a single.
Works it with the spin to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Easy pickings! Brathwaite fires it full and wide down the leg side, Kohli deflects it fine down the leg side and finds the rope.
Second new ball is available now. Not taken by Windies. Strange.

Miscommunication but no harm done! A very full ball on off, Rahane drives it firmly to mid off and sets off for a run. Kohli denies it as it has gone straight to the fielder and Rahane has to rush back.
Flighted and full on off, Rahane is on the front foot in defense.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flatter and on off, defended off the back foot.

FOUR! On the shorter side around off, Rahane immediately rocks back and cuts it through covers for a cracking boundary. Have lost count of the number of short ball lollies served to the Indian batsmen.
Fullish and on off, flicked across the line but straight to short mid-wicket.
A slider around middle, skidding away after landing, Rahane gets back and helps it in front of square leg for one.
This one is flat and short around leg, Kohli nudges it through square leg and picks up a single.
Another flick shot by Kohli finds the fielder at mid-wicket.
Too full and on middle, hit across the line but straight mid-wicket.
Loopy and around leg, Rahane rushes down the track and drives it through mid off for a run.
Full and flighted on middle, Rahane gets on the front foot and pushes it to the off side.
Skipper Kraigg Brathwaite brings himself into the attack. A slip and short mid-wicket in place.
Flighted and full on off, driven back to the bowler.
Tossed up ball on middle, Kohli plays it with the turn to mid-wicket.
Leans forward to a full ball and drives it to covers.
Works it with the spin on the leg side but finds the fielder.
FOUR! Shot! Tossed up ball around off, Kohli advances down the track and plays a wristy cover drive through the gap. Eye-soothing one. Change of gears perhaps.
Full flighted on off, flicked across the line but straight to short mid-wicket.

Drinks on the field, again. The Windies' search for a breakthrough continues. To be honest, their field setup is not for wicket-taking anyway. Quite defensive. The bowlers are lacking plans. What to say about India? They are cruising and nothing seems to stop them at the moment. 13 overs left in the day's play. Let's hope we get all of them bowled.
Flatter and shorter on off, stroked off the back foot to covers.
Driven through the covers by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Goes on the back foot and punches it to short mid-wicket.

Fifty for India's run-machine! Kohli is back in the team and he continues with his usual business. Run scoring has become a piece of cake for this batsman. Bishoo helps him there with a short delivery outside off, Virat rocks back and cuts it through point. The fielder chases it and just about manages to pull it back. The onfield umpire gets it checked upstairs and it's a clean stop. Strangely, the fielder himself was of the opinion that it was a boundary. Still the officials wanted to be extra sure. Hmm... Anyway, two runs taken and that's enough to bring Kohli's 20th Test fifty. A bit on the slower side, one can say, but maybe he wants to spend time in the middle after having a good rest.
A man drops back in the deep on the leg side.
Spinning away from the batsman around off, Kohli pushes it with the spin towards extra cover but not in the gap.
Flighted leg spinner dropping outside leg, Kohli defends it off his front foot.
Floated one, full and on off, Rahane is forward in defense.
Defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Short and outside off, Rahane cuts it off his back foot to point where the fielder attacks the ball and slips a bit. Still does well to not let it go.
Very full in length around off, Rahane drives it firmly down the ground but finds the mid off fielder.
Slower through the air, full and on off, Rahane leans forward and defends it back.
An off spinner, landing short around off and turning back in, Kohli gets back and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Loopy full delivery, landing around leg and spinning towards off, Rahane lunges and defends it compactly.
Straighter in line and shorter in length, Kohli goes on the back foot and pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Bishoo is not learning. Keeps it short and outside off, it's been cut with ease to sweeper cover for a single.
FOUR! Bishoo drops it short and around off, spinning away, Rahane goes back and cuts it through the line. It comes off the outer half of his blade and speeds away to the third man fence.
Flighted leg spinner on leg, from 'round the wicket, Rahane goes on the back foot and defends it on the off side.
Turns it on the leg side towards square leg and crosses for a hesitant single.
Pushes it back towards mid on and Chase stops it with a dive to his right.
Very full on off, driven off the front foot to the extra cover fielder.
Shortish and outside off, punched from the crease to point.
Helps it off his pads to square leg for a run.

Flatter and shorter on off, punched back towards the bowler. Chase moved across to his right to stop the ball but collided with Rahane a bit. Good thing for him was that the ball got deflected to short mid-wicket.
Lovely delivery, full and drifting in around off, Rahane is on the front foot and defends it with the spin to the off side.
Bowls this one with a quicker arm action, a leg spinner around off, on the shorter side, Rahane punches it off his back foot to covers.

A bit short and around off, spinning away, Kohli hangs back and punches it down the ground. He calls for a run and as soon as Lewis fails to cut it off with a dive from mid on, they pick up a couple more. 300 up for India!
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flighted and full on off, defended off the front foot.

Deft touch. Bishoo bowls a leg spinner which is on the shorter side around off. Kohli stands quietly inside the crease, waits for the ball to do its bit and then guides it last past first slip. Two runs added to the total.

While India continue to do well here, there is more good news filtering in, just across the border. The Indian colts have just progressed to the final of the Under-19 Asia Cup, beating Bangladesh by 2 runs. They have successfully defended a total of 172. Will meet either of Afghanistan or Sri Lanka in the final on Saturday.
Allows the ball to turn back in and works it off his back foot. Finds the gap at mid-wicket and retains strike with a single.
Goes back and helps it with the spin to square leg.
Quicker and on middle, defended on the leg side.
Kohli has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Gets on the front foot and plays it with the spin to mid-wicket.
Short and on middle, whipped off the back foot through mid-wicket for a couple.

Soft edge, not carrying to Shai Hope. Bishoo gets his length right for once in this over and lands it full on middle. Rahane is forward in defense but it spins away to take the outside edge. Since it's played with a soft bottom hand, the edge doesn't carry to first slip.

Yet another shorter delivery by Bishoo. Rahane is picking the length very early. Immediately camps back and cuts it through point. This time Ambris quickly gets across to his left in the deep and they take a couple.
Floated full ball on middle, once again defended back by Rahane.
Full and flighted on off, Rahane strides forward in defense.
Shortish and on off, turning away, Rahane gets back and defends it to the off side.

FOUR! A leg spinner on the shorter side, Rahane rocks back and whacks it through covers. The fielder in the deep sprints across to his right but fails to cut it off. Bishoo is not too happy with the effort put in by Ambris. Maybe, the bowler demanded a dive which didn't come.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Beaten! Flighted and outside off, not turning back in much, Kohli commits himself forward in defense, thinking it will turn back in but it skids on straight to beat the outside edge. A rare occurrence, this.
Steps down the track and eases it through mid on for a run.

EDGED AND FOUR! Just wide of first slip. Chase lands it short and around off, Rahane goes back to cut but it's too close to his body. He still goes on with the shot and gets it away off the outside edge. It flies past the outstretched right hand of Shai Hope and screams away to the third man fence.
Loopy off spinner on off, Rahane strides forward and blocks it safely.
Starts with a full toss on middle, it's knocked down past the diving short mid-wicket fielder to long on for a run.
Roston Chase is back on.
Keeps it full and outside off, once again a forward defensive shot on offer in this over.
Floated full ball on off, defended off the front foot by Rahane.
Bishoo is losing control over his length here. Serves a long hop again, outside off, Kohli cracks it off his back foot to sweeper cover for a single. 50-run stand comes up. Good going from India.
A tossed up delivery on middle, again a bit short in length, Kohli hangs back and hits it to deep mid-wicket for a couple.
As soon as Bishoo drags his length short, Rahane goes deep inside the crease and cuts it through point for a run.
Loopy and full on middle, a leg spinner, Rahane defends it off his front foot.
Reaches out for a length ball outside off and pushes it towards the fielder standing at cover-point.
Pitches it up and around off, Kohli plays the off drive but finds the fielder. Quite a few good shots have found the fielders. Slightly frustrating for the Indian skipper.
Lands it on a length and outside off, Kohli prods forward and pushes it to covers.
In better control this time, Virat. He clips a full ball off his pads to deep mid-wicket and returns for the second run.
Targets the off stump with a length delivery, Kohli is on the front foot in defense.
A bit uppish, that. A length ball landing around off and moving back in a bit, Kohli goes hard at it with his attempted flick shot and does so a bit aerially. It though rolls safely to mid on.
Loopy and on off, defended off the front foot to the off side.
Jumps out of the crease to a full ball around off and then offers a straight bat in defense. Got deceived in flight a bit, otherwise he was eyeing an aerial shot.
Tossed up ball on middle, blocked back off the front foot.
Full and flighted outside off, Kohli reaches out for it and drives it through covers for a run.
Kohli has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flighted and outside off, tapped down with the turn to point.
Good length delivery in the corridor of uncertainty, Rahane makes a watchful leave.
Fullish and on middle, Kohli pushes it gently down the ground and the mid on fielder moves across to his left to make the stop. A single picked.
Defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

A delightful stroke off the front foot by Kohli. His third drive in this over but once again he fails to find the gap. That cover fielder makes a diving stop to his right. Virat is outside his crease but sends his partner back seeing that effort. Called a no ball for overstepping.
A length ball outside off, Kohli pushes it with soft hands to covers. Maybe, wanted to drop and run but nothing doing.
This seems as if Paul is daring Kohli to pierce the off side field. Serves it full and wide outside off, Virat executes the drive but once again finds the cover fielder.
A length delivery outside off, Kohli gets on the front foot and drives it with good timing. But he fails to beat the cover fielder.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Short and outside off, cut through the covers. Good effort by Lewis, running to his right from point and putting in a dive. Two runs taken.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.

DRINKS BREAK. Things seemed to have quietened down since the dismissal of Shaw but India are firmly in the driver's seat. Both Kohli and Rahane look at ease and though neither are looking as commanding as the 18-year old, neither are struggling. Still 26 overs left in the day.
Pretty much wide outside off, there is no need to play at those. End of an innocuous over.
Pitches it up outside off, Kohli gets on the front foot and pushes it towards point.
Back of a length delivery outside off, left alone.
Gets on the front foot to a full ball and drives it to covers.
In the region outside off, the length is there to be driven but Kohli has nothing to do with it. Called a no ball for overstepping.
Another length ball is angled into the Indian skipper who keeps it out safely with a straight bat.
Starts the spell with a good length delivery on off, Kohli defends it off his back foot to the off side.
Keemo Paul is back on.
Tossed up and on off, defended off the front foot.
Leans forward to a full ball and drives it back to the bowler.
Goes on the back foot again and punches it towards covers.
Short and outside off, Rahane defends it off his back foot.
A bit short and on middle, Rahane goes on the back foot to play it down towards the leg side.
Floated and full around leg, Kohli leans forward and nudges it in front of square leg for a run.
Fullish and on off, Rahane drives it off his front foot back towards the bowler.

FOUR! And a shot like this will be demoralizing. Gabriel is struggling with his length. This time he is too full around off, Rahane just presents the full face of his willow as he eases his straight drive down the ground for a boundary.

Fuller in length and outside off, Rahane is on the front foot as he drives it through the line. The cover fielder dives to his right to take the pace off the ball and parries it towards mid off. No run taken. Good effort in the field. Stuff like this will keep them in good spirits.
Fullish and on off, it's clipped off the pads towards wide mid on. Straightaway a loud call for no by Rahane.
Digs in a short ball around off, Rahane is early into his pull shot and hence misses. It hits him on the shoulders and rolls behind to first slip.
Length ball angling in around off, Rahane pushes it down with an angled bat to point.
Flatter and shorter on off, punched to sweeper cover for a run.
The batsman helps it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Skidding down towards the leg side, Kohli works it through behind square and takes a brace.
Full and on off, driven off the front foot again, this time past silly point and straight to the cover fielder.
Ouch! That would have hurt. A flighted delivery, Kohli cracks it on the full and it hits the silly point fielder. The ball deflects to covers. No pain showed there by the fielder under the helmet.
A gentle harmless delivery, wide outside off, Rahane covers his stumps and allows it through.
Gabriel continues to be too straight with his line. Not looking threatening at all. Kohli works it around through square leg and rotates the strike.
Once again the length is a touch short around off, Rahane stays back, uses his wrists and turns it through square leg for a single.
Shortish on off, bowled at 144 kph, Rahane pushed it from the crease to covers. Looked for a run but was sent back.
Back of a length delivery on off, Rahane stands tall and plays it down towards short mid-wicket.
Slight stoppage in play. Some movement near the sightscreen probably.

Poor line again to begin the over. A length ball sliding down the leg side, Kohli nudges it off his pads through backward square leg. The fine leg fielder makes the stop by running across to his left and they take a run.
Nicely played. A flighted full ball on middle, Kohli flicks it past the left side of the mid-wicket fielder. The mid on fielder moves across to his right to stop the ball and the batsmen cross.
Loopy full ball down the leg side, Rahane sits down on on knee and paddles it behind square leg for a single.
Strides forward to a full ball and drives it through mid off for a single.
Quicker and fuller on middle, another front foot defensive shot offered by Virat.
The line is on middle stump this time, Kohli is on the front foot as he defends it with the spin.
Flighted leg spinner outside off, Kohli opts not to drive it with a slip in place waiting for an outside edge.
A length ball around off, angling towards the off stump, Rahane lunges and defends it comfortably.
Shortish and on off, Rahane goes on his toes and defends it to the off side.
Fuller in length and on off, angling in, Rahane is on the front foot as he pushes it back to the bowler.
Back of a length delivery on off, Rahane taps it down towards point and initially eyes a run. But he soon realizes that the placement is not good enough and hence shouts nooo.
This time both the line and length are wrong. It's full and on the pads, Kohli flicks it through square leg for a run.

Wrong length to begin with. An overpitched one on middle, at 146 kph, Rahane flicks it across the line and the mid on fielder rushes across to his right. He puts in a slide to stop the racing ball and the batsmen change ends.
Shannon Gabriel returns in the attack.
Flighted and full on middle, Rahane leans forward and defends it watchfully.
Turning away from the batsman from outside off, Rahane rocks back and cuts it through point for a single.
Just a bit short in length on this occasion, around middle and leg, Kohli goes deep inside the crease and works it through square leg for a run.
Too full and around middle, it's pushed back towards the bowler.
Presses forward to a full ball and defends it with a straight bat.
Tossed up ball around off, spinning away slightly, Kohli is on the front foot as he covers the line before leaving it for the keeper.
Shortish delivery outside off, it's bowled at a gentle pace, Kohli runs it down to third man for a run.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
Taps a length ball in the gap at covers for a single.
This time Kohli plays his flick shot wide of the mid-wicket fielder, to the right of him, to be precise. A single taken.
Full and angling in on middle, Kohli flicks but finds the mid-wicket fielder.

FOUR! Lovely timing and also a very ordinary fielding effort. Lewis pitches it up and around off, Kohli times his off drive to perfection as it races through. Gabriel rushes across to his left from mid off, puts in a late diving effort as it speeds past him to the fence.
Short in length and outside off, Rahane cuts it off his back foot but finds the point fielder.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Short this time by Bishoo, allowing the batsman to get back and punch it to sweeper cover for a run.
Extra flight this time, trying to tempt the batsman by bowling it full and on off, Kohli has nothing to do with it.
Tossed up ball on off, defended off the front foot to the off side.

Quicker and flatter one, skidding again off the surface, Rahane draws forward in defense and it takes the inside edge. Bishoo has his hands on his head in disappointment. The ball in the meanwhile rolls in the gap at square leg and they cross for a run.
Full and around off, shaping back in, Kohli gets on the front foot and defends it watchfully to end the over.
This one is too full and on off, Kohli digs it out off the inner half of the bat to mid on.
Bowls it on a length outside off, Kohli takes a big stride forward and pushes it to covers.
Lands it on a length and just around off, Kohli stays back and defends it off the inside half of his bat to the leg side.
The line is too straight once again and Rahane flicks it through square leg for one.
Angles in a length ball on off, Kohli clips it off the inner half of his bat to fine leg for a run.
Allows the ball to spin away and taps it down safely on the off side towards backward point.
Strides forward to a full ball and eases it through mid off for a run. Bishoo won't mind the batsman driving as there is turn on this surface and any mistake may result in an outside edge.
Bishoo drags his length back and bowls it around off. It skids off the surface after landing and Kohli punches it off his back foot to covers.
The length is very full on this occasion, around off, Rahane strokes it through covers for a run.
Too full in length on off, Rahane lunges and pushes it back to the bowler.
A little short and on off, spinning away, Kohli punches it in front of square on the off side and takes a single.
Devendra Bishoo to continue from this end...
Lewis gets away with one. Bowls a juicy full toss outside off, Rahane pushes it through the line but finds the cover fielder.
Angles in a length ball on off, Rahane remains on the back foot in defense.
Serves it on a good length outside off, Kohli plays it late and guides it wide of point for a run. The fielder square on the off side is stationed in the deep by Brathwaite. Strange tactics.
Hurls in a length delivery in the channel outside off, Kohli takes a stride forward to cover the line before making a leave.
Lewis digs in a short delivery this time, outside off, Kohli stands tall and plays it down towards the cover-point fielder.

FOUR! A delightful shot to get us underway. What a player! Receives a gentle half-volley on middle and caresses it straight down the ground with a nice flourish of his bat. So good to the eyes, Kohli with his straight drive.

The evening session is about to begin and we welcome you again for all the action. The Windies have two new batsmen in the middle and would like to dismiss them early. But the names of those two are Virat Kohli and Ajinkya Rahane, so easier said than done. Right? Sherman Lewis to kickoff proceedings. Two slips in place.
... DAY 1, THIRD SESSION ...

39 overs left in the day. If the Windies bowl all of these, I daresay my fingers are going to get quite some pain by the end. Realistically speaking, we are looking at the visitors falling 8-9 overs short. Brathwaite might have to opt for the spinners a bit more than usual to try and complete as many overs as possible. Join us back at 1430 local (0900 GMT).

The Windies have looked listless right after the first Drinks break. They have bowled an odd good ball here and there but simply have not been consistent. They will consider themselves lucky in taking two wickets. More pain might be there come the final session.

The Indians started this session from the word go, attacking the bowlers. Then, from nowhere, Windies got Pujara. Kohli then came in and closed the shutters a bit while the debutant continued his flow. But towards the end of the session, Bishoo managed to snap him. Looking at the score, the hosts will not be too concerned. 232/3 in just 2 sessions. With Kohli yet to get going. Pant to come. Jadeja to come. Anything apart from runs to come?

India's session without a doubt but just that wicket of Shaw in the dying moments takes some gloss off it. 99 runs came in 26 overs, for the loss of Pujara and Shaw. Both dismissals can be touted to loss in concentration, rather than excellent bowling.
Full and around off, Rahane closes the bat-face tightly and defends. TEA ON DAY 1.
Around off, watchfully blocked out.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Ajinkya Rahane walks in next, at number 5, replacing Shaw.

OUT! The debutant's fine show ends. Just moments before Tea. A nothing delivery, a nothing shot. Short ball, around off, Shaw goes back and looks to work it to the leg side. However, the ball stops on the pitch and now Prithvi looks to push it through the line. But he ends up chipping it tamely to Bishoo who takes it but so pulverized are the Windies that no one is celebrating. The Indians are silent too. Stunned, in fact. The way Prithvi was batting, it seemed like he was timing everything beautifully. A soft dismissal. Now, the entire crowd stands up like one to applaud. Well played, kid.
Misfield from Chase. The Windies are looking totally listless. A short ball, pulled through mid-wicket, straight to short mid-wicket. However, Roston Chase takes it easy and fumbles. A run allowed.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
Similar delivery, once again PS looks to defend on the front foot but this one does not turn. Goes past the outside edge.

ALMOST GETS BOWLED! Ashwin and Jadeja will like that. Full and outside off, Prithvi comes forward to defend but the ball spins in a long way, takes the inside edge and just goes over the stumps, past the keeper, to fine leg! The batsmen take two.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Full and outside off, not that much room. But Shaw still goes after it. Ends up slicing his shot and gets it over cover. The ball almost stops near the ropes but in the end, touches it.
Full on middle, pushed towards long on for a single.
Roston Chase is back on. 5-0-32-0 so far.
A short ball, pulled with aplomb through mid-wicket for a brace.
Full and around off, pushed past the bowler for a single towards mid off.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Tossed up outside off, Kohli lunges and blocks it towards mid-wicket.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off for a single.

Wild delivery. Wilder movement. Full and down the leg side, Prithvi is nowhere even close to making contact with that as he looks to flick. The ball goes further down the leg side and Shane Dowrich puts in a spectacular effort to dive to his left and get a glove to it. Parries it to fine leg and restricts the run scoring to a bye.
A bouncer now, Shaw ducks.
Outside off, on a length, punched straight to cover.
Off the mark on the 10th ball. Half volley on middle, VK flicks it through mid-wicket and gets a single.
Similar ball, once again Virat waits for the ball to come to him and then dabs it late towards point. Shaw wants the single but is sent back.
A length ball outside off, Kohli watches that from the crease and then plays it towards point.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Full and around off, watchfully pushed towards cover.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR! Too close for comfort. Short and outside off, Shaw goes back and looks to cut but is too close to the ball. Ends up getting a thick outside edge which flies past first slip, to the third man fence.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Devendra Bishoo is back on. 14-1-62-0 so far.
This is now wider on the other side. Left alone.
Down the leg side, Kohli misses out on another tickle.
Around off, solidly defended.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Around off, watchfully defended.

That is a beauty! Gabriel lands it on a length, around off, Shaw perhaps thought that it is a bouncer and wanted to duck. But then, he realized that the ball is not bouncing that much and hence he tries to work it to the leg side with a closed bat-face. In the end, got squared up and was lucky that the ball did not take the edge.
Around off, defended tightly.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.
Short and outside off, PS rises on his toes and slaps it towards sweeper cover. There is a man in the deep who runs to his right from point but the ball lands short of him. A single taken.
Landed outside off, dabbed towards gully.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
A bouncer on middle, Shaw ducks. An alert Sanjay Manjrekar on air observes that this is just the second time in this innings that Prithvi has ducked under it.
Another appeal, this time for a catch. Down the leg side, Kohli looks to tuck but misses. Dowrich gets across to his left and then appeals after taking that, but no bat.
Full and outside off, Kohli looks to defend but gets hit on the pads and then on the bat. Gabriel starts to appeal but the impact was outside off.
Down the leg side, flicked behind square leg for a single.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. Good effort by the fielder to save a certain boundary. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Outside off, pushed towards cover.
Shannon Gabriel is back on. 9-1-33-1 so far.
Skipper Virat Kohli walks in at number 4, replacing Pujara.

OUT! Caught behind! A rare glorious moment for the Windies as they prize out the 206-run stand. But a big moment for the debutant. Nothing special on the delivery, but just a lapse in concentration from the batsman. A length ball outside off, could have been left alone but Pujara has a flirt at it. Perhaps he wants to rotate strike and get to the other end. But then, he realizes that he can let the ball go. That indecision costs him and a thin outside edge is produced. The keeper pouches it and the Windies appeal but Pujara is not going! Now Ian Gould raises his finger and sends him on his way. The home lad will feel disappointed on missing out on a century. It was there for the taking.
Down the leg side, left alone.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
A bouncer on middle, Cheteshwar ducks.
Around off, that one kicks off the surface, Pujara is surprised but manages to fend it down.
Full and outside off, eased through the covers for a single. He wants the second but his partner is not the least bit interested.
Full and outside off, driven past cover for one.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a run.
Punches this off the back foot for a single.

FOUR! Short, wide, outside off, help yourself. And Shaw does exactly that. Rocks back and cuts it aerially behind point. THE 200-RUN STAND IS UP. Also, Shaw becomes the highest scorer in the first innings on Test debut for India.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full on middle, almost a yorker, dug out back to the bowler.
Outside off, played straight to point.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
FOUR! Another delightful shot. Short and outside off, Shaw waits for the ball to come to him and guides it behind point for a boundary. It is not all about saw for Shaw.
A short ball outside off, Shaw looks to cut but misses.
Full and outside off, solidly blocked towards cover.
Moral victory for the Windies. Another maiden has been bowled. Second in the last 6 overs. Full and outside off, CP lets it go.
Another long hop, Cheteshwar looks to cut but gets a bottom edge back to the bowler.
Outside off, left alone once again.
Landed outside off, let through.
On middle, punched down to mid on.
Landed outside off, slow but appreciable turn, watchfully let through.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
Pushes this towards mid on.
A short ball outside off, Pujara looks to cut but misses.

Is that the first time Shaw has missed out on scoring? By the looks of it, yes. The first leg bye in this innings. On a length, around middle and leg, Prithvi misses his tuck. He too, seems shocked that he has missed out on a scoring opportunity. Stands dead still for a moment before he is called through for a single.
Sherman Lewis is back into the attack. 5-0-34-0 so far.
Around off, watchfully blocked out.
Comes down the track and wrists this towards mid on.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They pick up a single.

Full and around off, Shaw drives this straight back. Bishoo tries to stop it with his right hand but deflects it towards mid on. Pujara, in an attempt to get back, dives back in his crease. Seeing the mid on fielder a bit wide, Prithvi wants a single but poor old Pujjy is taking a lonnnng time to get back onto his feet.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Thrown up wide outside off, driven straight to cover.
Full and outside off, pretty wide, left alone.

Oh dear. Not good. Not good at all. Keemo Paul is on his haunches and seems to be struggling with the heat. His teammates are surrounding him and the physio is out too. Doesn't look like cramps. More like dehydration. Very difficult to play in such conditions if one is not used to these. Meanwhile, the umpires take the opportunity to call for Drinks. India maintain their ascendancy post Lunch. 60 runs have come in just 11.5 overs. The good thing for India is that they have come from both ends, not from just Shaw's bat alone. He is on a different planet altogether and would like to see - when was the last time Pujara batted so quickly?

FOUR! SUBLIME! Overpitched on middle, Pujara comes forward and drives it straight back to where it came from. Once again, Shaw is down at the non-striker's end. Not because he is struggling but because he was trying to get back into his crease.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Around off and outside, pushed towards the leg side.
Tough for the bowler. Paul comes running in but at the last moment, Pujara backs away. Probably something or someone must have distracted him behind the sightscreen.
Full and around off, watchfully blocked out.
A length ball outside off, Pujara looks to cut but the ball probably stays a touch low. Gets a bottom edge which goes to the keeper on the bounce.
Goes back and works it through square leg for one. Moves to 80 now.
Outside off, punched down to long on for a run.
Don't think this bloke will allow any spinner to bowl a string of dots to him. Comes down the track and milks it through square leg for a single.
Full and outside off, defended to the off side.
Much better from Bishoo, keeps it fuller, Cheteshwar looks to defend but the ball goes off the inner half towards mid-wicket.
FOUR! That will be the 28th in this innings. Not for the first time have we seen Bishoo drop it short to Pujara. The local lad goes back and cuts it behind point. The stand is worth 183 now.
Similar ball, defended to the off side again. A rare maiden - JUST THE SECOND in this innings.
Around off, defended from the crease.
Full and just outside off, Prithvi is tight in defense.
Overpitched outside off, Shaw drives it beautifully but straight to cover.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Around off, defended from the crease.

WAS THAT A DROP? The keeper does not look too happy with himself. Neither is Bishoo. Short and outside off, Pujara rocks back and looks to cut but misses, at least from the first look to the naked eye. Shane Dowrich looks to grab it and Bishoo gets excited but then the keeper fumbles. Hard to say any edge from that angle.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They manage to come back for the second.
Full and around off, watchfully blocked out.
Comes down the track this time and defends.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.

FOUR! Gift. Short and outside off, turning away, Pujara goes back, waits for the ball to come to him and cuts it behind point. Lot of boundaries scored already. This is the 27th four in just the 34th over. Pujara himself has scored 12 of those in his 72.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Outside off, on a good length, holds its line, Pujara looks to defend, playing on the inside but gets beaten.
Outside off, eased behind point for a single.
Around off, Shaw stays back in his crease and blocks.

TEST TON ON DEBUT! 15th Indian to do so and only the second by an opener. 7th youngest centurion in Tests. A proud moment for him and even more for his teammates. Take a bow, Prithvi Shaw. He is just an 18-year old. Who knows, how many more will he have by the time his Test career ends? Too early to think about that. His career has just taken off. Coming to the ball, Shaw drives it through the covers and scampers back for the second. Takes his helmet off and then soaks in the applause. Virat Kohli cannot hide his glee. This is a thing about colts these days. They are not afraid of the situation or any challenge. He has been given an opportunity and he has accepted that with open arms.
Full on middle, blocked towards mid on.
Keemo Paul is back on. 4-0-28-0 so far.
Around off, tightly defended.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and around off, watchfully blocked.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.

ALMOST A RUN OUT! Smiles with relief in the Indian camp. Pujara was nearly made a sacrificial lamb there. On middle, Shaw goes back and works it towards square leg. He takes the single and then looks to come back for the second. Pujara responds but then is sent back. He stutters, looks to get back and eventually dives in.
Right then. Here comes the moment. Shaw on 98. Can he get to his century in this over?
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Back of a length delivery outside off, PS waits for the ball to come to him and dabs it behind point for a single.

FOUR! PRISTINE! Shaw is just a hit away from a century. Half volley outside off, Prithvi reaches out, gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it through the covers for a boundary. No protection in the deep.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Fractionally short outside off, coming in, Shaw looks to punch on the rise but the ball hits the inner half of his bat and rolls to mid on.

Just an update from the Under-19 Asia Cup. India are currently playing Bangladesh in Dhaka in the first semi-final and have recovered from 77/5 to post a competitive 172. On a slow and turning track, it will be interesting to see how the hosts respond. Afghanistan and Sri Lanka will feature in the other semi-final tomorrow.
Full and around off, watchfully blocked.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Comes down the track and defends.
Tossed up slowly outside off, Pujara watches the ball carefully, sees it spin away, goes back and then pushes it to the off side.
Outside off, this time Prithvi finds the gap at cover and gets a single.
Short and outside off, Shaw cuts it hard but straight to the man at cover.
Full on middle, driven straight to mid on.
A slower ball, full toss, down the leg side, 128 kph, Cheteshwar misses his flick. Probably the lack of pace did him in.
Full on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.

Good call from Pujara. A back of a length delivery outside off, Shaw backs away slightly and then guides it behind point. He takes the first run quickly and wants the second but that would have been suicidal. The fielder had already got to the ball and had the second been taken, a run out opportunity would have been created. Pujara sent Shaw back in time though.
Outside off, played behind point for a single.
Outside off, WOW. A rare sight since Lunch. LEFT ALONE.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.

FOUR! Dropped short, Shaw goes back and pulls it through square leg for another boundary. Rainy season is over in major parts of India but in Rajkot, it is raining. Only, instead of water drops, it is boundaries.
Full and around off, Shaw gets down and slogs it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Full on middle, flicked towards short mid-wicket.
Full on middle, pushed towards the bowler.
FOUR BYES! The runs keep on piling. Short and outside off, Bishoo looks to cut but misses. The keeper is beaten by the spin and bounce while first slip does not have even half a chance.
FOUR! A boundary to end the over. Half volley on middle, Pujara comes forward and whips it wide of Devendra Bishoo at mid on. 11 from the over.
Driven through the covers by the batsman. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs. 150-RUN STAND IS UP and the pair is showing no signs of tiring.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
FOUR! Easy pickings. On a length outside off, Pujara waits for the ball to come to him and dabs it to third man for a boundary.
Short and outside off, cut through point for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Shannon Gabriel to bowl from the other end. 6-1-15-1 before Lunch.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball towards long on. One run added to the total.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! More evidence of what is mentioned on the previous ball. A slightly short ball on middle, Shaw pulls it over mid-wicket and gets boundaries in succession!
FOUR! PLUNDERED! He is not letting any gears down. Full and outside off, Shaw gets down and mows it through mid-wicket for a boundary! Break or no break, this kid does not care.
Outside off, punched towards mid on.
Full and just outside off, Shaw defends watchfully.

Welcome back for the afternoon session. The men concerned are back on the field. Both the current Indian batsmen will be eyeing daddy hundreds with the way they are going. For Windies, they need a breakthrough immediately otherwise it will be a leather hunt for them. Devendra Bishoo to begin proceedings. A few fielders already placed in the deep and there is just one slip in a catching position. On the defensive, not good signs. Anyway, here we go...
... DAY 1, SECOND SESSION ...

Not surprisingly, the visitors look flat and decimated already. There are fielding lapses being seen and the bowling is being more on the shorter side. All this on just the opening session of a Test match. Hopefully, we get some competitive cricket in the second session.

When the ball stops moving after 5 overs, then you will never wish to be a bowler. Spare a thought for the Windies. The track is as flat as the national highway but full credit to Shannon Gabriel whose 6-0-15-1 stands out in this heat. The rest have been ordinary, including the spinners, who have not been able to exert some control.

The day started well for the Windies though, with Shannon Gabriel trapping Lokesh Rahul LBW in the very first over. But after that, it has been one-way traffic. Shaw just took the bull by the horns and did not allow any bowler to dominate, while Pujara, after consuming a few balls early on, has started to stamp his authority.

You don't need to be a rocket scientist to find out that this is India's session. 133 runs, at a run rate of more than 5 an over. More than half of those being scored by an 18-year old. Oh yes, it is India's present with the future looking more than good.
Full and down the leg side, flicked through mid-wicket for a brace. LUNCH ON DAY 1.
Back of a length outside off, Pujara gets on the back foot and steers it straight to gully.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Outside off, played towards point for a run.

EDGY FOUR! Too close for comfort. A short ball outside off, Shaw makes up his mind to play the cut but is cramped for room as the ball comes back in a long way. He gets a thick outside edge but because the second slip has been removed, the ball flies through the unmanned area. All the way to the third man fence.
On a length outside off, Pujara waits for the ball to come to him and dabs it towards third man for a single.
3 minutes to go for Lunch. Seems like Windies are not interested in even trying to get more than one over before the break. Here's Lewis.
Similar ball, this is flicked through square leg and the result is a couple. Shaw moves to 70 from 72 balls.
Full and down the leg side, flicked towards backward square leg.
On middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a quick, quick run. Not sure that is needed at this stage. Just 5 minutes for the breather.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman.
The batsman dances down the track but decides to defend it.
Full and outside off, Shaw drives it straight back to the bowler. Should have been stopped but Chase fumbles and concedes a single.

FOUR! 19th Test fifty for Cheteshwar Pujara! And it has come in just 67 balls. Consider this - he was on 2 from 21 deliveries. Surprisingly, this is just his first against Windies in 5 innings, with the previous 50-plus score crossing the 100-mark. Talking about the ball, Pujara comes forward and drives it past mid off and gets the boundary.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
Outside off, now he attempts the upper cut but misses.
FOUR! Cracking shot. Short and outside off, Shaw lashes out the cut and gets it behind point to find the fence.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Sherman Lewis is back on. 3-0-17-0 so far.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a couple.
Full and around off, watchfully blocked out.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
Full on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman dances down the track and does well to block the ball.

FOUR! Pristine timing and effective precision! There is a man at short mid-wicket and a man at deep mid-wicket. Yet Pujara, with an efficiency second to none, finds the gap and the boundary. Full and on middle, Cheteshwar comes down the track and whips it through that gap.
First flashy shot from Prithvi. Getting frustrated? A short ball outside off, Shaw slashes hard but misses.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
One more leave outside off.
Outside off, left alone.
On a length outside off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

NO BALL! The second in this session and both have been, not surprisingly, by You-Know-Who. Nope, he is not Voldemort, if any Harry Potter fans are reading this. Gabriel bends his back and stretches his foot by a bit more than the permissible margin. Pujara lets it through. That raises the century stand as well.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

FOUR! This is overpitched but the result is the same! Toying with the bowling, is Prithvi. Chase tosses this up outside off, Shaw comes forward and threads this through the covers. Moves to 61 from 62 balls with 9 boundaries.
FOUR! Bad bowling. Short and outside off, Shaw rocks back and punches it through the covers. There is a man in the deep, but he is at point. No point in even trying to chase.
Around off, wristed through mid-wicket for a run. Moves to 40 from 54 balls.
Landed outside off, pressed towards point for a single. The stand moves to 90 now.
Full and around off, worked towards short mid-wicket.
Short and outside off, thumped through the covers for one.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a run.
Slightly flashy from CP. A touch short outside off, the right-hander looks to cut but misses. No feet movement.
A bumper down the leg side, Pujara ducks.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
On a length outside off, Shaw punches it through backward point. The fielder from gully dives to his right and gets a hand to it, deflecting the ball towards third man. A single taken.
Shannon Gabriel is back on. 4-1-10-1 so far.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.
FOUR! Lovely shot. Full on middle, Pujara comes down the track and flicks it through mid-wicket. The fielder from long on hares to his right, puts in a dive but comes second best.

HALF CENTURY ON DEBUT! Just the 12th Indian opener to do so in his first innings. Already making raves and the class is there to see for all. Full on middle, Shaw pushes it towards long on and gets to the milestone. He has done the hard work. Now, for the temperament to make it count. Becomes the youngest debutant to score a fifty in Test cricket for India and the fifth youngest overall.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Now it is dropped short. Shaw goes back and plays his favourite shot - the punch. Gets it behind point where it is saved with a slide. Two runs taken.
Full and outside off, dabbed towards cover.
Much fuller and CP blocks.
Another long hop, this is outside off. Cheteshwar rocks back and pulls but finds short mid-wicket.
FOUR! We are now witnessing a boundary ball almost every over. A short ball, down the leg side, Pujara goes back and pulls it behind square leg for a boundary.
Landed outside off, played straight to point.
Eases this through mid off for a run.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Full on middle, wristed towards long on for a run.
Full and around off, Pujara is down the track again, only to defend.
The batsman dances down the track but decides to defend it.
Outside off, steered through point for a single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Roston Chase to bowl now.
The batsman has driven it through mid on. One run added to the total.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Very full outside off, squeezed behind point for a single.
FOUR! Easy peasy. Jumps out once again and whips it wide of mid-wicket for a boundary.
Jumps down the track and drives it back to the bowler.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. 10 runs from the over, the most expensive one in the this innings.
Down the leg side, flicked toward backward square leg for one.
Short and outside off, cut through point for a run.

FOUR! Finally a cover drive gets full justice. Half of his shots on the off side  have found fielders but this one finds the gap. Full and outside off, Shaw leans and drives it through the covers. The man dives to his right but in vain. The stand moves to 63 from 76 balls with Shaw reaching 42 from 42 deliveries.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! MARVELLOUS! The kid continues to impress. Half volley on middle, the opener drives it straight back. Mid on dives to his left, but in vain.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on for a single.
Short again, Shaw misses out once more. Cut straight to point.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. One run added to the total.
Full and outside off, left alone.

DRINKS. Prithvi Shaw's session. He has been in the news right from last afternoon and continues to be, with every ball that he is facing and every shot that he is playing. He has shown no signs of nerves at all and taken the attack to the opposition. Attack - yes. With a strike rate of 91.67 in a Test match, what else would you say? One of my colleagues, ABK, jokes - he looks like a combination of Sehwag and Tendulkar. The former for flair. The latter for class and temperament. Just so that you don't feel that this is a blog about Shaw, let us focus on the game a bit. Windies have been a mixed bag. When the ball was moving around a bit, they managed to get a wicket but in the last half an hour or so, they have been pretty flat, just like the track. With Pujara now getting amongst the runs, the run-rate is on the move. Not to mention, the over rate is appalling.
Outside off, tapped towards point for an easy single.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Slightly slower in pace, outside off, 128 kph, Prithvi reads it well. Waits for the ball to come to him and then dabs it towards point for a quick single.
On a length outside off, played towards cover.
Well outside off, pretty full toss, Shaw reaches out but then lets it go.
Full and outside off, driven beautifully but straight to mid off.
Keemo Paul is back on. 2-0-16-0 in his first spell. He replaces Lewis.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Short and outside off, punched through cover for a single.

FOUR! New-age player. What a way to bring up the 50-run stand. In just 58 balls. Full and outside off, tossed up a bit, Shaw leans and lofts it straight back over the bowler. The ball lands just inside the ropes near long off. Shaw moves to 31 from 31 balls and this is his fifth four.
Outside off, pushed to cover for a quick single.

FOUR! A short ball, down the leg side, Pujara initially looks to pull. But then, he is cramped for room a touch, probably because the ball spins in and bounces a touch. He now tries to adjust and attempts to lap it fine. As a result, gets a top edge which lands safely behind square leg. Finds the fence too. Moves to 20 from 28 balls. He was 2 from 18, not too long ago.
Works it through mid-wicket for a run.
A length ball outside off, Shaw gets on top of the bounce and punches it through point for a single. The stand moves to 40 from just 54 balls.
The ball is too wide on the off side for the batsman to make any contact.
Pushes this through point and gets a single.
FOUR! Third boundary in the last four balls for Pujara. Short and outside off, the local boy gets on top of the bounce and punches it through point. Finds the gap and the boundary.
Outside off, played through point for a single.
Pushes this through mid on and gets a single.
Around off, watchfully kept out.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Full and just outside off, watchfully defended.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Landed outside off, Shaw looks to cut but misses.
Spin time now. Devendra Bishoo is inserted.

FOUR! EVEN BETTER! Pujara is now getting into his stride. Full on middle, Cheteshwar drives this straight back. Shaw at the other end is nearly forced into a complete split as he falls flat on his back side. Pujara moves to 10 with 2 boundaries. The stand is worth 32 now.
A touch short this time, cut straight to point.
FOUR! MAJESTIC! The margin for error is a bare minimum on this track. Pretty full, around off, Pujara just gives it a bit of a direction. Past the non-striker and to the long on fence.
Much slower than the previous one, 134 kph shows the radar, Cheteshwar defends it back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, pretty fast, but a calm Pujara blocks.
A length ball outside off, played towards cover.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.
Down the leg side, flicked towards backward square leg for a run.
A full toss outside off, Pujara plays it late and finds point.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Already men have spread out for Shaw. Full and on middle, he flicks it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
A length ball wide outside off, left alone.
Similar ball, this is pushed towards point.
Just outside off, on a good length, watchfully blocked out.
A tad wide outside off, let through.
Fuller on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Short and wide outside off, punched towards deep point for a single.
Gentle loosener. Wide outside off, on a length, left alone.

Early bowling change. Sherman Lewis to bowl, replacing Keemo Paul. Not surprising, given that the latter went for 16 in 2 overs. The debutant is a right-arm pacer, with 49 wickets in First Class cricket, at an average of around 26 and a strike rate of close to 47. Got his Test cap from Ian Bishop earlier today. Lewis is the 316th player to represent Windies in Test cricket.
A length ball outside off, played towards point. FIRST MAIDEN OF THE TEST MATCH.
Full and just outside off, CP comes forward and pushes it towards cover.
A bouncer now, Cheteshwar ducks.
All the Windies players are wearing black-arm bands as a mark of respect for Kemar Roach's late grandmother who passed away earlier this week.
Full and just outside off, watchfully defended back to the bowler.
Similar ball, this time Pujara meets it with a full face of the bat by coming forward.
Full and outside off, coming in a long way, left alone.
