FOUR! Uppish but over the infield. Shaw is not letting any opportunity waste. Short and outside off, normally batsmen at this juncture of the game let balls go but not this kid. Flashes hard and gets a thick outside edge. Over gully and to the third man fence. Moves to 22 from 16 balls and this is his fourth boundary. The stand is now worth 21 from 19 balls.
Another fine punch, but finds point this time.
Outside off, punched towards cover.
FOUR! Badly lined. A length ball, down the leg side, Shaw just gives it a little tickle and finds the fine leg fence.
Full and outside off, driven sweetly but straight to point.
FOUR! On middle and leg, Shaw tucks it through mid-wicket. Sunil Ambris gives it a good chase from short mid-wicket, gets to the ball and then tries to pull it back, but in vain.
A length ball outside off, defended from the crease.
A slower ball, outside off, fuller in length, driven towards cover.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. Good running between the wickets to pick up three runs. Shaw moves to 10 at run-a-ball.

NO BALL! The first of hopefully, not many. Gabriel does not have a great history with overstepping. And he has made a mark in his second over straightaway. Oversteps by a big margin, just about touches the popping crease, lands it a touch short and Shaw ducks.
On middle and leg, helped towards fine leg for a single.
Around off, watchfully defended.

That is a jaffa. He has got his tail up for sure. The pace is up - AT 149 KPH. A length ball outside off, Pujara looks to play that from his crease but the ball comes back in a long way and goes right between bat and pad. Plenty of movement.
A length ball this time, punched square but finds point.
FOUR! First boundary for Shaw in Test cricket. Fractionally short outside off, Prithvi stands tall and punches it through cover to find the ropes!
Full on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Short and outside off, cut beautifully but point dives to his right to stop it.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
No warm-up. A bouncer around off, Shaw ducks.
In comes one of the local lads - Cheteshwar Pujara, pretty much earlier than he would have expected. Keemo Paul to bowl from the other end.

OUT! LBW! Waste of a review by Rahul. Gabriel has struck in the first over. Beauty of a delivery after a wasted first few balls. On a length outside off, Rahul puts in half a stride but fails to cover the line. The ball comes back in a long way and hits him flush on the pads. Gabriel appeals and appeals but umpire Ian Gould is not impressed. Eventually, after a long thought, he raises his finger. Rahul walks across to his partner, has a chat and then signals for the review. Bad choice. Hawk Eye shows the impact in line and the ball crashing into the middle and leg stumps. A blob for Rahul then. 5th overall in Tests but the second in his last 5 innings.
Howzzat? Rahul has been adjudged LBW. He has taken the review though. Looks plumb to the naked eye.
Outside off, played towards point.
Full and outside off again, lesser width, the batsman lets it go.
Excellent fielding! Full and wide outside off, Rahul reaches out and drives it behind point. But Shai Hope at gully dives to his right and makes a brilliant stop.

Shaw is up and running. And a nice way to do so as well. A length ball outside off, not as wide as the previous one, Prithvi gets on top of the bounce and punches it through the covers. The fielder from point gets to the ball, puts in a slide, pulls the ball back in but it rolls back towards the ropes. However, he dives after coming out and saves the boundary. Three runs taken.
A little bit of movement in the air, but a touch wide outside off, Shaw shoulders arms.

The anthems are done and the players make their way out to the middle. A big, big moment for Prithvi Shaw as he takes the field, ahead of Lokesh Rahul. Now, the Windies follow suit. Shannon Gabriel will make the first use of the new cherry. Shaw will face him. Amazing. Normally, the senior pro takes strike first up but not this kid. Here we go. Let's play!
Time for the national anthems. As is the tradition, the Windies' one is played first up.

Kraigg Brathwaite says that he also wanted to bat first. But now, hopes that his bowlers strike with the new ball and get some early wickets. Is eager to stay aggressive and enjoy the game. Informs that Jason Holder is missing out due to an ankle injury while Sunil Ambris comes back into the playing XI. Also tells that Sherman Lewis makes his Test debut for the Windies. On his unit doing well recently, Brathwaite hopes that the good run continues.

Virat Kohli says the surface is nice and dry and the grass is there to hold it together. Reckons that the conditions are good to play cricket as well and feels that the spinners will come into play on Day 3 and further. Feels sad for Shardul Thakur on missing out but is equally excited to see the young Prithvi Shaw and Umesh Yadav in the playing XI. On the team aim, Virat stresses that the basics should not be let go of - the batsmen need to get runs while the bowlers should not be letting their focus dip.

TOSS - We are all set for the spin of the coin. But big news - KRAIGG BRATHWAITE has come out in place of Jason Holder. Kohli flips the coin, Brathwaite calls Heads but it is a Tail. INDIA ELECT TO BAT FIRST.
WEATHER - The conditions are a bit murky with the sun yet to assume full heat. But needless to say, as the first session comes to a close, the players will feel the heat.

With India making a statement, announcing their twelve yesterday afternoon itself, they have gone even bolder by announcing the playing XI well before the toss. PRITHVI SHAW IS MAKING HIS TEST DEBUT while Shardul Thakur is the one missing out in this game. As for the Windies, we await their team news.

Test cricket is back in India! And it is inaugurated with Windies coming to the shores. A low-profile series it might be, but could make the careers for a few players from both sides. Prithvi Shaw for India. Sunil Ambris for the Windies, if selected. Also, a chance for the Indian batsmen to tune up before the tour to Australia. And, a chance for the tourists to show that they can provide a better future for their country in this sport. Hello and a warm welcome to the opening Test of the 2-match series between India and Windies in Rajkot.
